name: orb_5min_5s
author: adapted from claude-4.6-opus-fast
thesis: The 5-minute opening range (high and low of 09:15-09:20) captures the initial price discovery auction. Breakout above/below this range with volume confirmation signals institutional direction for the session. The 5-min ORB is the fastest variant — it works best on high-conviction gap days where institutions have clear directional intent from pre-open orders. The inefficiency exists because most retail traders are still deciding whether to trade during the first 5 minutes, missing the institutional flow signal. The 5-min range is narrow enough that false breakouts are frequent (~55% fail), so the edge comes entirely from asymmetric payoffs: winners run 2x+ losers.
mechanism: The opening range concentrates pending orders and stop-losses on both sides. When price breaches the range boundary, stop-loss orders from wrong-side participants cascade, amplifying the move. Breakout-following algorithms detect the breach and add momentum, creating a self-reinforcing move that typically persists for 60-180 seconds before the order book absorbs the flow.

conditions: close > vwap (above VWAP for additional confirmation)

exit.signal_exit: if NIFTY reverses > 0.5% against trade direction, exit (macro headwind)

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX between 12 and 22 (need vol for breakout but not chaos)
filters.expiry_filter: skip on F&O expiry day; skip if stock has earnings today

weaknesses: The 5-minute range is very narrow (often 0.2-0.4%), making it susceptible to noise-driven false breakouts; win rate is below 50%
On low-gap days (<0.2%), the 5-min range is compressed and nearly any price movement triggers a breakout, most of which fail
The strategy requires very fast execution (within seconds of breakout) to avoid slippage; delayed entry significantly reduces the reward-to-risk ratio
prior_art: Crabel (1990) 'Day Trading with Short-Term Price Patterns'; Fisher (2002) 5-min ORB. Indian market ORB studies by Choudhary & Saini (2015).
adaptation_notes: Converted from 1min to 5s bars. Lookback multiplier: 12x. Adaptations: timeframe scaling to 5-second candles; signal conversion from individual stock to NIFTY/BANKNIFTY index; lookback period scaling for 5-second bars; stop/target recalibration for 5-second timeframe. Stop/target calibrated for options point-based exits. Universe narrowed to NIFTY index.
